81:     def __init__(self, file_register, mosaic, stack_dimension='layer_id', stack_coords=None, space_dims=None):
82:         """
83:         Constructor of `GeoTiffReader`.
84: 
85:         Parameters
86:         ----------
87:         file_register : pd.Dataframe, optional
88:             Data frame managing a stack/list of files containing the following columns:
89:                 - 'filepath' : str
90:                     Full file path to a geospatial file.
91:                 - 'layer_id' : object
92:                     Specifies an ID to which layer a file belongs to, e.g. a layer counter or a timestamp. Must
93:                     correspond to `stack_dimension`.
94:                 - 'tile_id' : str
95:                     Tile name or ID to which tile a file belongs to.
96:         mosaic : geospade.raster.MosaicGeometry
97:             Mosaic representing the spatial allocation of the given files. The tiles of the mosaic have to match the
98:             ID's/names of the 'tile_id' column.
99:         stack_dimension : str, optional
100:             Dimension/column name of the dimension, where to stack the files along (first axis), e.g. time, bands etc.
101:             Defaults to 'layer_id', i.e. the layer ID's are used as the main coordinates to stack the files.
102:         stack_coords : list, optional
103:             Additional columns of `file_register` to use as coordinates. Defaults to None, i.e. only coordinates along
104:             `stack_dimension` are used.
105:         space_dims : list, optional
106:             Dictionary containing the spatial dimension names. By default it is set to ['y', 'x'].
107: 
108:         """
109:         super().__init__(file_register, mosaic, stack_dimension=stack_dimension, stack_coords=stack_coords)
110: 
111:         ref_filepath = self._file_register['filepath'].iloc[0]
112:         with GeoTiffFile(ref_filepath, 'r') as gt_file:
113:             self._ref_dtypes = gt_file.dtypes
114:             self._ref_nodatavals = gt_file.nodatavals
115: 
116:         self._ref_space_dims = space_dims or ['y', 'x']
117: 
118:     @classmethod
119:     def from_filepaths(cls, filepaths, mosaic_class=MosaicGeometry, mosaic_kwargs=None, tile_kwargs=None,
120:                        stack_dimension='layer_id', **kwargs):
121:         """
122:         Creates a `GeoTiffDataReader` instance as one stack of GeoTIFF files.
123: 
124:         Parameters
125:         ----------
126:         filepaths : list of str
127:             List of full system paths to a GeoTIFF file.
128:         mosaic_class : geospade.raster.MosaicGeometry, optional
129:             Mosaic class used to manage the spatial properties of the file stack. If None, the most generic mosaic will
130:             be used by default. The initialised mosaic will only contain one tile.
131:         mosaic_kwargs : dict, optional
132:             Additional arguments for initialising `mosaic_class`.
133:         tile_kwargs : dict, optional
134:             Additional arguments for initialising a tile class associated with `mosaic_class`.
135:         stack_dimension : str, optional
136:             Dimension/column name of the dimension, where to stack the files along (first axis), e.g. time, bands etc.
137:             Defaults to 'layer_id', i.e. the layer ID's are used as the main coordinates to stack the files.
138:         kwargs : dict, optional
139:             Key-word arguments for the `GeoTiffReader` constructor.
140: 
141:         Returns
142:         -------
143:         GeoTiffReader
144: 
145:         """
146:         mosaic_kwargs = mosaic_kwargs or dict()
147:         tile_kwargs = tile_kwargs or dict()
148: 
149:         n_filepaths = len(filepaths)
150:         file_register_dict = dict()
151:         file_register_dict['filepath'] = filepaths
152:         file_register_dict['tile_id'] = ['0'] * n_filepaths
153:         file_register_dict[stack_dimension] = list(range(1, n_filepaths + 1))
154:         file_register = pd.DataFrame(file_register_dict)
155: 
156:         ref_filepath = filepaths[0]
157:         with GeoTiffFile(ref_filepath, 'r') as gt_file:
158:             sref_wkt = gt_file.sref_wkt
159:             geotrans = gt_file.geotrans
160:             n_rows, n_cols = gt_file.shape
161: 
162:         tile_class = mosaic_class.get_tile_class()
163:         tile = tile_class(n_rows, n_cols, sref=SpatialRef(sref_wkt), geotrans=geotrans, name='0', **tile_kwargs)
164:         mosaic_geom = mosaic_class.from_tile_list([tile], check_consistency=False, **mosaic_kwargs)
165: 
166:         return cls(file_register, mosaic_geom, stack_dimension=stack_dimension, **kwargs)
167: 
168:     @classmethod
169:     def from_mosaic_filepaths(cls, filepaths, mosaic_class=MosaicGeometry, mosaic_kwargs=None,
170:                               stack_dimension='layer_id', **kwargs):
171:         """
172:         Creates a `GeoTiffDataReader` instance as multiple stacks of GeoTIFF files.
173: 
174:         Parameters
175:         ----------
176:         filepaths : list of str
177:             List of full system paths to a GeoTIFF file.
178:         mosaic_class : geospade.raster.MosaicGeometry, optional
179:             Mosaic class used to manage the spatial properties of the file stacks. If None, the most generic mosaic will
180:             be used by default.
181:         mosaic_kwargs : dict, optional
182:             Additional arguments for initialising `mosaic_class`.
183:         stack_dimension : str, optional
184:             Dimension/column name of the dimension, where to stack the files along (first axis), e.g. time, bands etc.
185:             Defaults to 'layer_id', i.e. the layer ID's are used as the main coordinates to stack the files.
186:         kwargs : dict, optional
187:             Key-word arguments for the `GeoTiffReader` constructor.
188: 
189:         Returns
190:         -------
191:         GeoTiffReader
192: 
193:         """
194:         mosaic_kwargs = mosaic_kwargs or dict()
195:         file_register_dict = dict()
196:         file_register_dict['filepath'] = filepaths
197: 
198:         tile_ids = []
199:         layer_ids = []
200:         tiles = []
201:         tile_idx = 0
202:         tile_class = mosaic_class.get_tile_class()
203:         for filepath in filepaths:
204:             with GeoTiffFile(filepath, 'r') as gt_file:
205:                 sref_wkt = gt_file.sref_wkt
206:                 geotrans = gt_file.geotrans
207:                 n_rows, n_cols = gt_file.shape
208:             curr_tile = tile_class(n_rows, n_cols, sref=SpatialRef(sref_wkt), geotrans=geotrans, name=str(tile_idx))
209:             curr_tile_idx = None
210:             for tile in tiles:
211:                 if curr_tile == tile:
212:                     curr_tile_idx = tile.name
213:                     break
214:             if curr_tile_idx is None:
215:                 tiles.append(curr_tile)
216:                 curr_tile_idx = tile_idx
217:                 tile_idx += 1
218: 
219:             tile_ids.append(curr_tile_idx)
220:             layer_id = sum(np.array(tile_ids) == curr_tile_idx) + 1
221:             layer_ids.append(layer_id)
222: 
223:         file_register_dict['tile_id'] = tile_ids
224:         file_register_dict[stack_dimension] = layer_ids
225:         file_register = pd.DataFrame(file_register_dict)
226: 
227:         mosaic_geom = mosaic_class.from_tile_list(tiles, check_consistency=False, **mosaic_kwargs)
228: 
229:         return cls(file_register, mosaic_geom, stack_dimension=stack_dimension, **kwargs)

231:     def read(self, bands=1, band_names=None, engine='vrt', n_cores=1,
232:              auto_decode=False, decoder=None, decoder_kwargs=None):
233:         """
234:         Reads data from disk.
235: 
236:         Parameters
237:         ----------
238:         bands : tuple of int or int, optional
239:             The GeoTIFF bands of interest. Defaults to the first band, i.e. 1.
240:         band_names : tuple of str or str, optional
241:             Names associated with the respective bands of the GeoTIFF files. Defaults to None, i.e. the band numbers
242:             will be used as a name.
243:         engine : str, optional
244:             Engine used in the background to read data. The following options are available:
245:                 - 'vrt' : Uses GDAL's VRT format to stack the GeoTIFF files per tile and load them as once. This option
246:                           yields good performance if the mosaic is stored locally on one drive. Parallelisation is applied
247:                           across tiles.
248:                 - 'parallel' : Reads file by file, but in a parallelised manner. This option yields good performance if
249:                                the mosaic is stored on a distributed file system.
250:         n_cores : int, optional
251:             Number of cores used to read data in a parallelised manner (defaults to 1).
252:         auto_decode : bool, optional
253:             True if data should be decoded according to the information available in its metadata. Defaults to False.
254:         decoder : callable, optional
255:             Function allowing to decode data read from disk.
256:         decoder_kwargs : dict, optional
257:             Keyword arguments for the decoder.
258: 
259:         """
260:         bands = to_list(bands)

@staticmethod
    def _read_tile_attrs(filepath):
        """Read the spatial attributes needed to construct a tile from a NetCDF file."""
        with NetCdf4File(filepath, 'r') as nc_file:
            return nc_file.sref_wkt, nc_file.geotrans, nc_file.raster_shape

    @classmethod
    def _tile_from_filepath(cls, filepath, tile_class, name, **tile_kwargs):
        """Create a mosaic tile from the spatial attributes of a NetCDF file."""
        sref_wkt, geotrans, (n_rows, n_cols) = cls._read_tile_attrs(filepath)
        return tile_class(n_rows, n_cols, sref=SpatialRef(sref_wkt), geotrans=geotrans,
                          name=str(name), **tile_kwargs)

    @classmethod
    def _mosaic_file_register_and_tiles(cls, filepaths, mosaic_class, stack_dimension):
        """Create the file register entries and tiles for a mosaic of NetCDF files."""
        file_register_dict = dict()
        file_register_dict['filepath'] = filepaths

        tile_ids = []
        layer_ids = []
        tiles = []
        tile_idx = 0
        tile_class = mosaic_class.get_tile_class()
        for filepath in filepaths:
            curr_tile = cls._tile_from_filepath(filepath, tile_class, tile_idx)
            curr_tile_idx = None
            for tile in tiles:
                if curr_tile == tile:
                    curr_tile_idx = tile.name
                    break
            if curr_tile_idx is None:
                tiles.append(curr_tile)
                curr_tile_idx = tile_idx
                tile_idx += 1

            tile_ids.append(curr_tile_idx)
            layer_id = sum(np.array(tile_ids) == curr_tile_idx)
            layer_ids.append(layer_id)

        file_register_dict['tile_id'] = tile_ids
        file_register_dict[stack_dimension] = layer_ids
        file_register = pd.DataFrame(file_register_dict)

        return file_register, tiles

115:         mosaic_class : geospade.raster.MosaicGeometry, optional
116:             Mosaic class used to manage the spatial properties of the file stack. If None, the most generic mosaic will
117:             be used by default. The initialised mosaic will only contain one tile.
118:         mosaic_kwargs : dict, optional
119:             Additional arguments for initialising `mosaic_class`.
120:         tile_kwargs : dict, optional
121:             Additional arguments for initialising a tile class associated with `mosaic_class`.
122:         stack_dimension : str, optional
123:             Dimension/column name of the dimension, where to stack the files along (first axis), e.g. time, bands etc.
124:             Defaults to 'layer_id', i.e. the layer ID's are used as the main coordinates to stack the files.
125:         kwargs : dict, optional
126:             Key-word arguments for the `NetCdfReader` constructor.
127: 
128:         Returns
129:         -------
130:         NetCdfReader
131: 
132:         """
133:         mosaic_kwargs = mosaic_kwargs or dict()
134:         tile_kwargs = tile_kwargs or dict()
135: 
136:         n_filepaths = len(filepaths)
137:         file_register_dict = dict()
138:         file_register_dict['filepath'] = filepaths
139:         file_register_dict['tile_id'] = ['0'] * n_filepaths
140:         file_register_dict[stack_dimension] = list(range(n_filepaths))
141:         file_register = pd.DataFrame(file_register_dict)

143:         tile_class = mosaic_class.get_tile_class()

145:         mosaic_geom = mosaic_class.from_tile_list([tile], check_consistency=False, **mosaic_kwargs)
146: 
147:         return cls(file_register, mosaic_geom, stack_dimension=stack_dimension, **kwargs)

182:     def read(self, data_variables=None, engine='netcdf4', parallel=True, auto_decode=False,
183:              decoder=None, decoder_kwargs=None):
184:         """
185:         Reads NetCdf data from disk and assigns it to the class.
186: 
187:         Parameters
188:         ----------
189:         data_variables : list, optional
190:             Data variables to read. Default is to read all available data variables.
191:         engine : str, optional
192:             Engine used in the background to read NetCDF data. The following options are available:
193:                 - 'netcdf4' : Uses the netCDF4 library to create an `MFDataset` object.
194:                 - 'xarray' : Uses xarray's `open_mfdataset` function.
195:         parallel : bool, optional
196:             Flag to activate parallelisation or not when using 'xarray' as an engine. Defaults to True.
197:         auto_decode : bool, optional
198:             True if NetCDF data should be decoded according to the information available in its metadata. Defaults to
199:             False.
200:         decoder : callable, optional
201:             Function allowing to decode NetCDF data read from disk.
202:         decoder_kwargs : dict, optional
203:             Keyword arguments for the decoder.
204: 
205:         """
206:         data_variables = to_list(data_variables)
207:         new_tile = Tile.from_extent(self._mosaic.outer_extent, sref=self._mosaic.sref,
208:                                     x_pixel_size=self._mosaic.x_pixel_size,
209:                                     y_pixel_size=self._mosaic.y_pixel_size,
210:                                     name='0')
211:         if engine == 'netcdf4':
212:             data = self.__read_netcdf4(new_tile, data_variables=data_variables, auto_decode=auto_decode,
213:                                        decoder=decoder, decoder_kwargs=decoder_kwargs)
214:         elif engine == 'xarray':
215:             data = self.__read_xarray(new_tile, data_variables=data_variables, parallel=parallel,
216:                                       auto_decode=auto_decode, decoder=decoder, decoder_kwargs=decoder_kwargs)
217:         else:
218:             err_msg = f"Engine '{engine}' is not supported!"
219:             raise ValueError(err_msg)
220:

220: 
221:         Returns
222:         -------
223:         RasterData :
224:             Raster data object with a mosaic and a file register in compliance with the provided select operations.
225: 
226:         """
227:         if not inplace:
228:             new_raster_data = copy.deepcopy(self)
229:             return new_raster_data.select(cmds, inplace=True)
230: 
231:         for cmd in cmds:
232:             fun_name = cmd[0]
233:             args = cmd[1]
234:             kwargs = cmd[2]
235: 
236:             sref = kwargs.get('sref')
237:             if sref is not None:
238:                 sref = SpatialRef(sref)
239:                 kwargs['sref'] = sref
240: 
241:             getattr(self, fun_name)(*args, inplace=True, **kwargs)
242: 
243:         return self

300:     def select_px_window(self, row, col, height=1, width=1, inplace=False):
301:         """
302:         Selects the pixel coordinates according to the given pixel window.
303: 
304:         Parameters
305:         ----------
306:         row : int
307:             Top-left row number of the pixel window anchor.
308:         col : int
309:             Top-left column number of the pixel window anchor.
310:         height : int, optional
311:             Number of rows/height of the pixel window. Defaults to 1.
312:         width : int, optional
313:             Number of columns/width of the pixel window. Defaults to 1.
314:         inplace : bool, optional
315:             If True, the current raster data object is modified.
316:             If False, a new raster data instance will be returned (default).
317: 
318:         Returns
319:         -------
320:         RasterData :
321:             Raster data object with a data and a mosaic geometry only consisting of the intersected tile with the
322:             pixel window.
323: 
324:         Notes
325:         -----
326:         The mosaic will be only sliced if it consists of one tile to prevent ambiguities in terms of the definition
327:         of the pixel window.
328: 
329:         """
330:         if not inplace:
331:             new_raster_data = copy.deepcopy(self)
332:             return new_raster_data.select_px_window(row, col, height=height, width=width, inplace=True)
333: 
334:         if self._data_geom is not None:
335:             self._data_geom.slice_by_rc(row, col, height=height, width=width, inplace=True, name='0')
336:             if self._data_geom is None:
337:                 wrn_msg = "Pixels are outside the extent of the raster mosaic."
338:                 warnings.warn(wrn_msg)
339: 
340:         if len(self._mosaic.all_tiles) == 1:
341:             tile_oi = self._mosaic.all_tiles[0]
342:             tile_oi.slice_by_rc(row, col, height=height, width=width, inplace=True, name='0')
343:             tile_oi.active = True
344:             self._mosaic.from_tile_list([tile_oi], inplace=True)
345: 
346:         return self

348:     def select_xy(self, x, y, sref=None, inplace=False):
349:         """
350:         Selects a pixel according to the given coordinate tuple.
351: 
352:         Parameters
353:         ----------
354:         x : number
355:             Coordinate in X direction.
356:         y : number
357:             Coordinate in Y direction.
358:         sref : geospade.crs.SpatialRef, optional
359:             CRS of the given coordinate tuple. Defaults to the CRS of the mosaic.
360:         inplace : bool, optional
361:             If True, the current raster data object is modified.
362:             If False, a new raster data instance will be returned (default).
363: 
364:         Returns
365:         -------
366:         RasterData :
367:             Raster data object with a file register and a mosaic only consisting of the intersected tile containing
368:             information on the location of the time series.
369: 
370:         """
371:         if not inplace:
372:             new_raster_data = copy.deepcopy(self)
373:             return new_raster_data.select_xy(x, y, sref=sref, inplace=True)
374: 
375:         if self._data_geom is not None:
376:             row, col = self._data_geom.xy2rc(x, y, sref=sref)
377:             self._data_geom.slice_by_rc(row, col, inplace=True, name='0')
378:             if self._data_geom is None:
379:                 wrn_msg = "Coordinates are outside the spatial extent of the raster mosaic."
380:                 warnings.warn(wrn_msg)
381: 
382:         tile_oi = self._mosaic.xy2tile(x, y, sref=sref)
383:         if tile_oi is not None:
384:             row, col = tile_oi.xy2rc(x, y, sref=sref)
385:             tile_oi.slice_by_rc(row, col, inplace=True, name='0')
386:             tile_oi.active = True
387:             self._mosaic.from_tile_list([tile_oi], inplace=True)
388:             self._file_register = self._file_register[self._file_register['tile_id'] == tile_oi.parent_root.name]
389:         else:
390:             wrn_msg = "Coordinates are outside the spatial extent of the raster mosaic files."
391:             warnings.warn(wrn_msg)
392:             return
393: 
394:         return self
